extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political theory / comparative government (including American readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and assessing the institutional features, strengths, and weaknesses of small republican governments (cantons, leagues, city-republics) with emphasis on whether they are truly democratic or mixed. The page provides descriptive criteria and normative remarks used to judge constitutions and political arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: citizen_participation_and_attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: A general or too common disinclination to attend leaves room for persons and parties more active to carry points by passion and intrigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, regular attendance by citizens is necessary to prevent small active factions from steering government; absenteeism undermines the democratic character of institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: legislative_composition_and_membership_rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Half nobles, half plebeians — all upwards of five-and-twenty years old — 'two thirds must agree — no son can sit with his father; never two of the same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate legislatures by their formal composition (social mix), age minima, supermajority requirements, and anti-nepotism rules; these structural details are used as checks and limitations on legislative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: separation_of_powers_allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The capitaneos have the executive, like the Roman consuls, and the community has the judicial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether executive, legislative, and judicial functions are distinct and which bodies hold them — clear separation is taken as evidence of a balanced/mixed constitution rather than a simple democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: judicial_independence_via_appointment_and_terms
rubrics_metrics.description: He must be a foreigner, and he is for three years. This is to give some degree of stability to the judicial power, and to make it a real and powerful check both to the executive and legislative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider special appointment rules (e.g., requirement that a judge or magistrate be a foreigner, fixed terms) intended to stabilize the judiciary and make it an effective check on other powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: mixed_constitution_indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a mixture of monarchy, aristocracy, and democracy ... the powers of the governor, senate, and assembly are more exactly ascertained and nicely balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether a government blends monarchical, aristocratic, and democratic elements; presence of multiple distinct orders and internal balances indicates a mixed constitution, not a pure democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: sovereignty_vs_government_form
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of sovereignty in all nations is unalienable and indivisible ... the exercise as well as right of sovereignty in Rome resided in the people, but the government was not a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish legal sovereignty (who holds the right) from the actual institutional form of government; possession of sovereignty by the people does not automatically make the regime a pure democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: property_distribution_and_absence_of_hereditary_nobility
rubrics_metrics.description: In America ... they have the whole property of land. There are no nobles or patricians — all are equal by law and by birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether land/property distribution and the absence of hereditary nobility support democratic equality; such socioeconomic facts are relevant to judging the democratic character of a polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: frequency_of_elections_and_term_lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: The governors and senates, as well as representative assemblies, to whom the exercise of sovereignty is committed, are annually chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, regular terms (e.g., annual elections) are indicators of democratic responsiveness; compare term lengths and rotation practices across institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: internal_division_within_legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislature itself is divided into monarchical, aristocratical, and democratical branches; and an equilibrium has been anxiously sought for in all their deliberations and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for internal subdivisions of the legislative function intended to represent different interests/orders — these are judged as mechanisms to achieve balance and prevent domination by any single order.

rubrics_metrics.name: scale_and_population_suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: A handful of poor people, living in the simplest manner ... can be no example for the commonwealth of Pennsylvania, Georgia, or Vermont ... a stronger proof cannot be adduced of the necessity of different orders, and of an equilibrium between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether an institutional arrangement that works in a tiny, homogeneous community is suitable for larger, more populous states; models that function at small scale may not scale up without introducing orders and balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: small_scale_personal_acquaintance_reduces_tyranny_risk
rubrics_metrics.description: In so small a state, where every man personally knows every other, ... it is scarcely possible that anything like tyranny or cruelty can take place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate risk of tyranny partly by social size and intimacy: personal knowledge among citizens is seen as a natural check on abuse of power in very small communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: economic_conditions_and_office_compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: The poverty of this people appears, by the fine of one penny imposed upon absence from the arengo; and by the law, that an ambassador should have a shilling a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe how low salaries, fines, and economic circumstances shape civic behavior and office-holding; economic poverty influences the character and costs of public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: eligibility_restrictions_and_de_facto_aristocracy
rubrics_metrics.description: They must be elected ... out of a few noble families, untainted ... must be natives and residents, worth a thousand ducats, and must have no concern in commerce, manufactures, or trade ... Thus we see the people themselves have established by law a contracted aristocracy, under the appearance of a liberal democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize formal eligibility requirements (birth, religion, wealth, ban on trade) that restrict office-holding; such rules can convert nominally democratic institutions into oligarchies/aristocracies in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: propensity_to_division_and_fragmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The disposition to division, so apparent in all democratical governments, however tempered with aristocratical and monarchical powers, has shewn itself, in breaking off from Guipuscoa and Alaba:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess democratic polities for tendencies toward factionalism and secession; democratic systems may be more prone to internal divisions unless checked by other orders or external constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: local_autonomy_and_subdivision_governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the government is called a democracy, we cannot here find all authority collected into one center; there are ... as many distinct governments as there are cities and merindades. Each subordinate division has its organized government, with its chief magistrate at the head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree of decentralization: multiple autonomous local bodies and subnational governments indicate a confederated or federal character and diffuse sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: composition_and_frequency_of_central_assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: The government resides sovereignly in the commons, where everything is decided by the plurality of voices. The commons elect and instruct their deputies for the general diet, which is held once a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check how often central assemblies meet, how deputies are selected and instructed, and whether decisions are by plurality or weighted voting — these procedural details affect representativeness and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: universal_male_suffrage_at_young_age_in_local_assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereignty resides in the general assembly, where all the males of fifteen have entry and suffrage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note direct participatory rules (e.g., male suffrage from age 15) for village/canton assemblies; such provisions indicate a high degree of direct popular participation at local level.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiple_councils_and_chambers_as_checks
rubrics_metrics.description: They have one general sovereign council ... the grand council ... the little council, called the weekly council, because it meets every week ... chambers of seven and fifteen for justice and police.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the presence of multiple deliberative bodies with different compositions and meeting frequencies — these are institutional checks and mechanisms of specialization (finance, justice, police).

rubrics_metrics.name: selection_by_combination_of_election_and_lottery
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner of his appointment is a mixture of election and lot. The people choose five candidates, who draw lots for the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate selection procedures that mix election and sortition as a method to balance popular choice with randomness to limit factional capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: religious_and_regional_quota_representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The senate ... composed of sixty-two senators, forty-eight Protestants and fourteen Catholics, all taken from fifteen tagwen ... In this senate ... the executive power resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess executive/regulatory bodies for formal quotas or proportional guarantees across religious or regional groups — these are accommodations aimed at stability and legitimacy in plural societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: normative_outcomes_public_tranquillity_and_general_happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberty, independence, and an exemption from taxes, amply compensate for a want of the refinements of luxury ... As the end of government is the greatest happiness of the greatest number, saving at the same time the stipulated rights of all, governments like these ... deserve to be admired and imitated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge regimes also by outcomes: preservation of public tranquillity, general happiness of the majority, protection of rights, and avoidance of licentiousness are normative metrics for good government.

rubrics_metrics.name: risk_of_concentration_and_need_for_balance_as_state_grows
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, however, but imperfectly balanced; so much of the executive power in an aristocratical assembly would be dangerous in the highest degree in a large state. If this canton could extend its dominion, or greatly multiply its numbers, it would soon find the necessity of giving the executive power to the landamman, in order to defend the people against the senate; for the senate ... is eternally the very focus of ambition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how institutional arrangements scale: concentrations of power tolerable in small polities can become dangerous as population and territory grow; anticipate institutional reforms (stronger executive) needed to maintain order and check ambitious aristocratic bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: confederal_character_vs_single_centered_authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A free republic, it is rather a confederation of four or five republics, each of which has its monarchical, aristocratical, and democratical branches, than a simple democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether a polity is truly centralized or effectively a confederation of smaller political units; the latter implies multiple centers of authority and complex inter-unit arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: practical_impossibility_of_simple_democracy_by_representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeed a simple democracy by representation is a contradiction in terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the conceptual point that representative institutions necessarily introduce mediation and orders; pure/simple democracy (representation-based) is deemed incoherent and in practice replaced by mixed or compound forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: necessity_of_orders_checks_and_balances_even_in_small_states
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a diminutive republic ... is interesting ... as it shews the impossibility of erecting even the smallest government, among the poorest people, without different orders, councils, and balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the presence of multiple orders, councils, and checks not as optional but as practically necessary features of stable government even in the smallest, poorest communities.
